 Cohere is the leading security\-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting\-edge foundation AI models and end\-to\-end products that are designed to solve real\-world business problems.
   

  

 We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.
   

  

 We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.
   

  

 We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!
   

  

**Why this role?**
 The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.
   

  

**In This Role, You Will**
* Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.
* Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.
* Work with researchers and training\-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements
* Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time\-to\-insight as the measures of success


**You May Be a Good Fit If You Have**
* Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.
* Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other
* Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.
* Hands\-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX\-style filesystems.


**It’s a Bonus If You Have**
* Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.
* Familiarity with the data\-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large\-scale model training.
* An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.

**About The Program**
The Alarm.com Software Rotation Program is a structured, cohort-based experience designed for exceptional early-career engineers who want to build deep technical expertise across Alarm.com's most strategic product areas. Over the course of three years, participants complete multiple technical and customer focused rotations before transitioning into a Software Engineer role.
  
  
This is not a traditional early-career role. We are looking for engineers who are intellectually curious, technically rigorous, and eager to contribute meaningfully from day one. Each rotation is a genuine team placement with real ownership — participants are embedded engineers, not observers.
  
  
A core principle of this program is building engineers who understand Alarm.com's customers as deeply as they understand the code. Participants will be intentionally exposed to customer-facing projects throughout their rotations — learning to evaluate technical decisions not just for correctness, but for the real-world impact they have on the millions of homeowners, businesses, and service providers who rely on Alarm.com every day.
  
  
This position is part of a cohort-based program. To ensure all participants begin rotations together and receive a consistent onboarding and development experience, employment for all cohort members begins on a single, unified start date.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Across all rotations, program participants will:
  
  

* Design, implement, and test new software features with full engineering ownership
* Contribute to the innovation and improvement of existing products and systems
* Analyze functional requirements and translate product specifications into quality software
* Research, evaluate, and integrate emerging technologies relevant to each rotation area
* Take ownership of assigned projects and drive them to completion on schedule
* Collaborate with QA, product, and cross-functional engineering teams on testing and deployment
* Deliver end-of-rotation presentations to leadership, demonstrating technical growth and business impact
* Engage with customer-facing product areas to develop a deep understanding of end-user needs — learning how engineering decisions directly shape the experience of Alarm.com's customers
* Apply a customer-first lens when designing and evaluating solutions, considering usability, reliability, and real world impact alongside technical correctness
* Participate in customer feedback reviews, product discussions, and cross-functional sessions that connect engineering work to the people it serves
* Other duties as assigned

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline
* 0+ years of professional software development experience (internship experience counts)
* Demonstrated ability to write clean, thoughtful, well-tested code
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a tenacious, self-directed work style
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills — ability to explain technical ideas clearly to varied audiences
* Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment
* Passion for building high-quality consumer technology products
* Genuine curiosity about AI, IoT, and the intersection of software and hardware
* Ability to think through the customer lens — genuine interest in understanding how your work affects real people, and willingness to engage with product feedback, customer context, and end-user outcomes
* Available to begin employment on the designated cohort start date (see above)
* Travel as needed to meet rotation requirements and temporary relocation (housing provided)

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience or coursework in machine learning, computer vision, or AI-adjacent domains
* Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, or platform engineering
* Previous relevant internship(s) in software engineering, applied AI, platform/infrastructure, or a related technical discipline — candidates with hands-on industry experience in areas aligned to our rotation tracks are strongly preferred
* Contributions to open source projects or a strong personal/academic project portfolio
* Experience working on or directly adjacent to customer-facing features, products, or support — any role where understanding the end user was part of the job

**What You Can Expect**

* Dedicated mentor and rotation manager throughout the program
* Regular 1:1s, mid-rotation check-ins, and structured performance feedback
* Presentation skills coaching and executive exposure opportunities
* Networking with Engineering Directors and senior leadership
* A clear, structured path to Software Engineer position
* Rotations outside of a traditional software engineering career path

**Who Are We Looking For?**
Vestwell is expanding and we’re keen to add an amazing Data Science role to our team. Someone who’s passionate about maths and algorithms to extract deep insights from large data sets, who will work primarily with our Cortex/AI solution, implementing ML and predictive analysis to help Vestwell see further into both the past and the future. We’re looking for someone who loves to solve problems and is driven to build great solutions. You will work across all our product lines - translating end-user needs into focused, actionable steps, that result in timely data products. You will help refine and execute our product vision, improving the requirement-intake process, and implementing new processes on a quarterly basis. Vestwell is a continuously evolving data engine at its heart.

* Understand high-level strategic initiatives and stakeholder requirements; identify opportunities; and translate inputs into buildable features with clear benefits
* Effectively communicate and share plans and rationales
* Partner with developers to break down product requirements into discrete tasks with clear functional requirements/acceptance criteria
* Provide constant and iterative feedback to the development team, including identifying bugs and assisting in resolution
* Complete functional testing and provide initial product sign-off when features are ready for end-user verification
* Develop processes and tools for tracking usage trends and allow data to inform future development plans

**Requirements**
The Necessities
  
  

* Graduate degree in data science or heavily-weighted category
* Ability to define and plan overall ML strategy with our Technical Director
* Ability to define and write algorithms
* 2-3+ years of Product Management experience
* Exceptional business and systems analysis skills
* Ability to work in a fast-paced, project-oriented environment to meet deadlines under tight time constraints
* Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment consisting of Product, Engineering, and QA resources
* Excellent communication skills, both in verbal and written formats
* Must have the ability to interface with internal stakeholders
* Ability to write/design python and/or R statistical programming

The Extras
  
  

* Data warehousing experience (Snowflake or Databricks)
* Actuarial experience

This role will be based in either the New York, Austin, King of Prussia, or Scottsdale office, and will be part of Vestwell's hybrid in-office operation.

We’re an innovative, high-growth company with an exciting future ahead. Make it rain. Make Snow. Make Earth Habitable. 

Rainmaker builds and deploys audacious technologies that work with nature to create an abundant, habitable planet. We are modernizing proven cloud-seeding science with weather-resistant UAS, radar and satellite observations, numerical weather prediction, novel sensing and validation systems, and sustainable seeding technologies. We are building an integrated system to make more freshwater available to farms, ecosystems, and communities.

Our ambition is bold, but we pursue it with humility. We take on difficult problems in the real world with technical rigor, grit, integrity, and an openness to learning and course-correcting. We are hiring individuals with evidence of exceptional ability. If you want to build systems that endure, restore, and deliver the future we were promised, we want to hear from you.

 The vehicle software team builds the software that operates Rainmaker’s cloud-seeding vehicles, connecting flight control, onboard computing, sensors, payloads, and ground operations. We work closely with electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and flight operations teams to turn new hardware into reliable systems that can be built, deployed, and operated at scale. Our goal is to make every vehicle a dependable tool for delivering more freshwater where it is needed.

About the Role

 - You will own vehicle software capabilities from the operator interface to the onboard systems that execute a mission. Your work will span ground stations, mission planning and execution, failsafe behaviors, sensing, payload and sensor integration, and autonomy. You will build software that helps operators make good decisions, lets vehicles carry out missions reliably, and handles failures predictably. You will take projects from architecture and prototyping through simulation, hardware integration, flight testing, deployment, and field support. We’re looking for a high-agency engineer who identifies what needs to happen, turns incomplete requirements into a clear plan, and follows through until the system works reliably in real operating conditions. This is a hands-on technical ownership role with the autonomy to shape the vehicle software and the responsibility to deliver it.

What You'll Do 

 - 

 - Own the architecture, implementation, and maintenance of vehicle software capabilities across onboard computers and ground systems, with clear contracts for commands, telemetry, state, and failure behavior.  

 - Build operator interfaces and ground-station workflows for vehicle preparation, preflight checks, mission control, health monitoring, and intervention. Make vehicle state, command outcomes, and required operator actions clear.  

 - Develop mission planning and execution software that turns operational goals into validated flight paths and geofences, accounts for vehicle endurance, coordinates flight and seeding activity, and supports mission changes as conditions evolve.  

 - Design and validate arming checks, interlocks, and failsafe behaviors for communication loss, degraded sensing, low power, process failures, and unexpected vehicle states, including clear transitions between autonomous behavior and operator control.  

 - Integrate sensors, cameras, and seeding payloads with onboard software and flight-control systems. Ensure measurements, calibration, timestamps, device health, and payload commands are reliable and observable.  

 - Develop autonomy that uses sensing and vehicle state to execute missions within operating limits, handle contingencies, and reduce operator workload.  

 - Build dependable communication between vehicles and ground stations, accounting for intermittent links, stale telemetry, and commands that may be delayed, duplicated, or unacknowledged.  

 - Build automated tests, software-in-the-loop simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop coverage that catch regressions and exercise failure modes before releases reach the fleet.  

 - Partner with hardware engineers and flight operations to validate new capabilities on the bench and in flight, and make deployment, configuration, calibration, and diagnostics repeatable.  

 - Investigate field failures using logs, telemetry, and mission replay; resolve root causes and turn what you learn into better software, tests, and operator workflows.

What We're Looking For

 - 

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience developing software for vehicles, robotics, or other systems that interact with the physical world, including deployment into production or field use.  

 - Demonstrated ownership of a software capability from design through integration, release, and ongoing support, including making technical decisions independently and resolving failures in real operating conditions.  

 - Strong systems programming skills in Rust or C/C++, with the willingness to work primarily in Rust and contribute to TypeScript-based operator interfaces. Our stack includes Rust onboard services and ground-station backends, React/TypeScript interfaces in Electron, and PX4 flight-control integration over MAVLink.  

 - Experience developing and debugging software on Linux, including concurrent processes, network communication, and interfaces to hardware or flight-control systems.  

 - Practical experience in one or more of the following: operator interfaces and ground stations, mission planning, autonomy, sensing, or payload integration, with the willingness to work across these boundaries.  

 - The ability to reason about distributed system state, timing, and failures, and implement robust state machines, fault detection, failsafes, and recovery paths.  

 - A practical approach to operator-facing software: you can turn field workflows into clear controls, useful feedback, and predictable system behavior.  

 - Experience building maintainable software with version control, reproducible builds, automated testing, and disciplined release practices.  

 - Evidence of high agency: you surface problems without waiting to be assigned, make sound decisions with incomplete information, ask for help when it matters, and close the loop on results.  

 - Clear communication and the ability to work closely with hardware engineers and operators, explain tradeoffs, and document decisions so others can operate and support what you ship.

What Will Set Your Apart

 - 

 - Experience deploying drones or autonomous robots and supporting real-world flight or field operations.  

 - Familiarity with PX4, MAVLink, ground-control systems, or flight-critical software.  

 - Experience building operator interfaces with React, TypeScript, or Electron, particularly mapping tools or geospatial mission-planning workflows.  

 - Experience with sensor fusion, state estimation, path planning, or autonomous mission execution.  

 - Experience integrating payloads, sensors, or embedded controllers over interfaces such as CAN, serial, or Ethernet.  

 - Experience validating safety-related behaviors through simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, fault injection, and field testing.

What Success Looks Like In the First 90 Days

 - You understand how operators plan and execute missions and can trace commands, telemetry, and failure behavior between the ground station, onboard software, flight controller, sensors, and payloads. You have identified the most consequential reliability risks and operator pain points, and the team has a clear plan for what to address first. You have delivered a meaningful vehicle software improvement through simulation and integration testing into an operational release, working with flight operations to verify its behavior in the field. You have demonstrated both its intended behavior and its response to relevant failures, and improved at least one recurring source of friction in mission planning, operation, testing, deployment, or diagnostics.

Supporting the Rainmakers behind the mission

Making earth more habitable is ambitious work and we want the people doing it to feel supported:

 - A stake in what we build: Meaningful stock options and the opportunity to help shape Rainmaker as an early member of the team. 

 - Support for your health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family. 

 - An investment in your future: A 401(k) with employer matching to help you build long-term savings. 

 - Time to recharge: Unlimited PTO for rest, exploration, and the people and pursuits that matter to you plus a generous paid holiday schedule. 

 - Time for a growing family: Paid parental leave for both parents to welcome a child and spend time together. 

 - Lunch together: Daily lunch provided at our El Segundo headquarters, giving Rainmakers a chance to share a meal and connect with teammates. 

 - Help making the move: Relocation assistance for eligible roles to support your transition to Rainmaker.

Rainmaker provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and for other protected reasons as required by law. If you need accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, contact hiring@makerain.com. You will contribute to applications and services that process market, position, and reference data and help enable risk calculations such as sensitivities/Greeks, VaR, PFE, and XVA.

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run.  Build software and deliver customer outcomes.  You’ll have the rare opportunity to gain deep insight into and directly influence some of the world’s most critical industries and institutions.  You have two internship role options.
   

  

**Forward Deployed Software Engineer**
 At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head\-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world\-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
   

  

 FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business\-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them.  As an FDSE Intern, you’ll experience the autonomy of a startup, with the resources, mentorship, and stability of an established tech company.
